widgets_values:
Cinematic environmental portrait of an elderly Swiss watchmaker
in his late seventies, sitting at a cluttered wooden workbench
inside a small traditional watch repair workshop.

Deep facial wrinkles, weathered skin, silver-gray hair,
short unkempt beard, thin metal-framed glasses resting low
on his nose, intense concentration in his expression.

His aged hands carefully assembling a tiny mechanical
watch movement using precision tweezers, intricate exposed
gears, miniature screws and delicate brass components.

The workbench is covered with antique pocket watches,
magnifying lenses, precision instruments, scattered watch
parts and worn leather tool cases.

Hundreds of old clocks and watches fill the shelves
behind him, creating a rich, authentic environment.

Warm tungsten light from an adjustable desk lamp
illuminates his face and hands, contrasting with cool
natural daylight entering through a dusty workshop window.

Subtle atmospheric dust particles, realistic reflections
on polished metal, aged wood grain, authentic skin texture,
natural imperfections, documentary photography,
cinematic composition, exceptional material realism,
rich tonal depth, physically accurate lighting,
35mm full-frame photography, 50mm lens, f/2.8,
subtle film grain, photorealistic.
